title: Final test: lessons 11–21
description: From forms and CSS to the DOM, events and fetch. 25 minutes, 5 of the 20 tasks are writing code. No points: −100 XP per mistake, leaving the test −2000 XP.

questions.prompt: A click on the word «I agree». What happens?
options: The box gets ticked — the input is inside the label
Nothing — the label has no for
Nothing — the checkbox has no id
questions.explain: If the field is inside the label, the link works without for and id.

questions.prompt: Box A grows on hover. What happens to box B below it?
options: It stays in place — A overlaps it
questions.explain: transform changes only the element's picture; its place in the flow stays the same. Neighbors don't move.
b = a copies the number. Then b changes on its own; a stays 3.
These are two separate ifs, not else if. Both are checked and both are true.
After 1 comes −2, and −2 > 0 is false, so the loop stops.
A variable declared inside a function lives only inside it. To get the value outside you need return.
map creates a new array; the original doesn't change.
find returns the first matching object. The first one older than 20 is Igor.
city is inside address. Correct: user.address.city.

questions.prompt: The page has three paragraphs with class item: «1», «2», «3». What's left after the code?
questions.explain: querySelector finds only the first matching element.

options: Error — a list of elements has no style
Only the first one turns red
questions.explain: querySelectorAll returns a list. A list has no style; you need to go through it with forEach.

questions.prompt: The paragraph already has the class active. Which classes will it have?
questions.explain: The first toggle removes the class, the second brings it back.

questions.prompt: What happens when the button is clicked?
options: Hello is printed once on load, clicks do nothing
questions.explain: sayHi() with brackets calls the function right away, and the listener gets its result, undefined. You need sayHi without brackets.

questions.prompt: The user clicks the word «bread». What happens?
options: Only the word «bread» is crossed out
questions.explain: e.target is the deepest element clicked. A click on «bread» is a click on <b>.

questions.prompt: A form with a task list, the button is type="submit". What happens on click?
options: The task flashes and disappears — the page reloads
The task is added and stays
questions.explain: There's no e.preventDefault() — the form submits and the page reloads.

questions.prompt: How many new <li> appear on the page?
questions.explain: The element exists only in memory. To show it you need list.append(li).
fetch immediately returns a promise, not data. A promise has no name field. The data is only inside .then.

questions.prompt: In what order do the numbers appear?
questions.explain: fetch doesn't wait for the reply: the code goes on and prints 3 right away. The server reply comes later — then 2 is printed.
In JSON keys and strings use only double quotes, and a trailing comma is not allowed.

options: Error data.forEach is not a function
questions.explain: data is an object, and objects have no forEach. The array is in data.results.
